name: NHS & respiratory
value: Flu above baseline and rising (wk 45 data)
summary: UKHSA 12 Nov: flu now above baseline and rising, at low levels; COVID-19 stable; RSV hospital admissions rising
state: UKHSA's report of 12 Nov, covering 2–8 Nov, says influenza activity increased and is now above baseline, circulating at low levels: hospital admissions rose to 3.65 per 100,000 from 3.00 and GP consultations to 7.3 from 6.2 (UKHSA). COVID-19 is stable at low levels, and RSV hospital admissions rose to low levels. Activity above baseline and rising meets the Watch line; no widespread NHS critical incidents were found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Older people, young children, pregnant women and people with long-term conditions are most at risk as flu rises. The NHS and UKHSA advise eligible people to get flu and COVID-19 vaccines; NHS 111 gives advice on symptoms.
rubric_hit: Watch: UKHSA says flu activity above baseline and rising (hospital admissions 3.65/100k, up from 3.00)

why: Winter respiratory waves and NHS capacity directly affect access to care for everyone in the UK.

rubric.alert: High or very high flu activity nationally, or widespread critical incidents.
rubric.watch: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising, or several trusts in critical incidents.
rubric.normal: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.
